name: OpenAI
product: GPT and reasoning-model APIs, ChatGPT, Codex, enterprise agents and multimodal generation.
targetCustomer: Consumers, developers, startups, enterprises and public-sector organizations
buyer: CTO, CIO, product and engineering leaders; individual users
fundingDisplay: $122B committed in the March 2026 financing; lifetime funding is not cleanly consolidated publicly
traction: Company-reported 900M weekly ChatGPT users, 50M consumer subscribers, more than $2B monthly revenue and API traffic above 15B tokens per minute in March 2026.
notes: Fact: the latest round and operating metrics are company-reported. Inference: scale, distribution and the developer ecosystem form the strongest combined moat in this cohort. Unknown: audited revenue and an unduplicated lifetime-funding total.

sources.label: OpenAI — Accelerating the next phase of AI

name: Anthropic
product: Claude models, consumer and enterprise assistants, coding agents and an API delivered directly and through major clouds.
targetCustomer: Developers, enterprises, regulated organizations and consumers
buyer: CTO, CIO, engineering, security and product leaders; individual users
fundingDisplay: $65B Series H announced in May 2026; lifetime total is not safely additive because the round includes previously committed investments
latestRound: $65B Series H at $965B post-money valuation, May 2026
traction: Company-reported annualized revenue run rate of $47B in May 2026, with Claude distributed directly and through AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.
notes: Fact: round size, valuation and revenue run rate come from Anthropic. Inference: safety positioning matters commercially only where it converts into reliability, governance and procurement wins. Unknown: audited revenue, customer concentration and unduplicated lifetime funding.

name: xAI
subsector: General-purpose foundation models and consumer assistant
product: Grok models, consumer assistant, API and real-time AI experiences integrated with X.
buyer: Individual users, developers, CTO and product leaders
fundingDisplay: $20B Series E before its February 2026 acquisition by SpaceX; lifetime standalone funding not consolidated
latestRound: Acquired by SpaceX, February 2026; prior $20B Series E, January 2026
traction: xAI reported roughly 600M monthly active users across X and Grok at the end of 2025. It is now part of publicly listed SpaceX rather than an independent startup.
notes: Fact: xAI announced the Series E and SpaceX combination; SpaceX's prospectus confirms the acquisition. Inference: X distribution and vertically owned compute are the core moat. Unknown: standalone xAI economics after the combination.

name: Cohere
product: Command language models, Embed and Rerank retrieval models, North enterprise-agent platform and private deployment options.
targetCustomer: Large enterprises, governments and regulated industries
buyer: CIO, CTO, CISO, data and AI platform leaders
fundingDisplay: Approximately $1.5B total raised; excludes an announced but not yet closed 2026 structured-financing commitment
latestRound: $600M across two 2025 closes ($500M in August and $100M in September)
traction: Le Monde reported about 500 employees and roughly $100M annual revenue in January 2026; Cohere names Oracle, Dell, RBC, Bell, Fujitsu, LG CNS and SAP among customers or partners.
notes: Fact: Cohere closed $600M in 2025 and emphasizes enterprise-private deployment. The approximately $1.5B total is a secondary estimate. Inference: its wedge is governance and deployment control rather than consumer distribution. Unknown: the terms and closure of the announced 2026 financing tied to Aleph Alpha.

sources.label: Le Monde interview with Cohere leadership

name: Mistral AI
product: Open and commercial language and multimodal models, Le Chat, API platform and private enterprise deployments.
buyer: CTO, CIO, AI platform and engineering leaders; individual users
fundingDisplay: €1.7B Series C in 2025 plus $830M debt financing in 2026; mixed-currency lifetime total not consolidated
latestRound: $830M debt financing for AI data-center build-out, March 2026
traction: Mistral had roughly 350 employees in September 2025 and offers API, assistant, open-weight and private-deployment products; audited commercial metrics are not public.
notes: Fact: ASML led the €1.7B Series C and Reuters reported the later debt financing. Inference: European sovereignty, open weights and private deployment create a differentiated enterprise wedge, but hyperscaler model competition is intense. Unknown: current revenue and exact unduplicated capital raised.

sources.label: ASML strategic partnership and Series C investment

name: Black Forest Labs
product: FLUX image-generation and editing models distributed through APIs, open weights and enterprise integrations.
targetCustomer: Creative software vendors, developers, media teams and consumers
fundingDisplay: $300M Series B in December 2025; lifetime total not consolidated in the primary announcement
traction: The company reports millions of FLUX users and distribution or product relationships with Adobe, Canva, Meta and Microsoft.
notes: Fact: the Series B, valuation and named integrations are company-reported. Inference: model quality plus broad developer distribution is a real wedge, but visual-model commoditization can compress API margins. Unknown: revenue, retention and total capital raised.

name: H Company
product: Vision-language action models and autonomous agents for browser, desktop and enterprise workflows.
targetCustomer: Enterprises with repetitive computer-based operations and developers building agents
buyer: COO, CIO, digital-transformation and automation leaders
traction: Public design-partner evidence includes FDJ and a Handicap International deployment monitoring roughly 13,000 information sources; broad production economics remain undisclosed.
notes: Fact: the company launched enterprise and consumer agent products after an unusually large seed round. Inference: its defensible asset must become action data and workflow reliability, not merely a generic agent interface. Unknown: paid production deployments, task-success rate and gross margins.

sources.label: H Company product launch and backing

name: Poolside
subsector: Code foundation models and software-engineering agents
product: Enterprise coding models, code agents and a platform deployable in private and air-gapped environments.
targetCustomer: Large software organizations and regulated enterprises
buyer: CTO, VP Engineering, CIO and developer-platform leaders
fundingDisplay: $626M total raised, including a $500M round in October 2024
traction: Poolside has released Laguna coding models and a private-deployment platform; it says its training method learns from execution feedback across more than 130,000 codebases, but revenue is not public.
notes: Fact: the $500M round, model releases and on-premises deployment are public. The $626M cumulative figure is a credible secondary estimate. Inference: code execution feedback and private deployment are the core moat hypotheses. Unknown: paid customer count, retention and outcome advantage over frontier general models.

name: Liquid AI
product: Liquid Foundation Models optimized for low-latency cloud, on-device and embedded inference.
targetCustomer: Enterprises, device makers, commerce platforms and developers with latency or privacy constraints
buyer: CTO, AI infrastructure, product and edge-platform leaders
fundingDisplay: $250M Series A in December 2024; lifetime total not consolidated in primary sources
traction: A multi-year, multi-million-dollar Shopify partnership targets sub-20ms commerce models; the agreement is stronger evidence than model benchmarks but does not establish broad adoption.
notes: Fact: funding, model releases and the Shopify partnership are public company announcements. Inference: architecture-level efficiency can be durable if it converts into measured cost and latency wins across hardware. Unknown: independent benchmark replication, revenue and customer concentration.

name: World Labs
product: Marble generates persistent, explorable 3D worlds from text, images and video, with creator and developer interfaces.
targetCustomer: Game, VFX, design, robotics and simulation developers
buyer: Creative-technology, product, simulation and R&D leaders
fundingDisplay: Approximately $1.23B total raised: $230M launch financing plus $1B in February 2026
traction: Marble is publicly available and produces persistent 3D environments from multiple input modes; commercial usage and revenue are not disclosed.
notes: Fact: World Labs announced $1B in new funding and ships Marble. The cumulative total combines its initial round reported by TechCrunch with the primary 2026 announcement. Inference: spatial consistency and editable 3D output are more defensible than generic image generation if they become production infrastructure. Unknown: paid adoption and unit economics.

name: Thinking Machines Lab
subsector: Model adaptation and frontier multimodal systems
product: Tinker managed fine-tuning API and research toward more customizable, understandable multimodal AI systems.
targetCustomer: AI researchers, model developers and advanced enterprise AI teams
buyer: Research, machine-learning platform and engineering leaders
latestRound: $2B seed at a reported $12B valuation, July 2025
traction: Tinker reached general availability and added vision support in late 2025; customer and revenue metrics remain undisclosed.
notes: Fact: the company now has a shipping fine-tuning product after raising a $2B seed. Inference: the defensible thesis is simplified access to frontier-scale training infrastructure and proprietary adaptation methods. Unknown: product-market fit, revenue and whether the lab will build its own base model.

sources.label: Thinking Machines Lab news and product updates

name: Safe Superintelligence
product: Pre-commercial research program focused exclusively on safe superintelligence; no public product or API.
fundingDisplay: Approximately $3B total across a $1B 2024 round and a $2B 2025 round
latestRound: $2B private financing at a reported $32B valuation, 2025
traction: No product, customer, revenue or public technical artifact sufficient to validate commercial traction as of July 2026.
notes: Fact: SSI explicitly prioritizes one research goal and remains pre-product. Inference: current moat is almost entirely founder and research talent, not validated technology or distribution. Unknown: model progress, commercialization path, deployment architecture and timing.

name: AMI (Advanced Machine Intelligence)
product: Pre-product world-model research aimed at persistent memory, reasoning and planning for physical and complex domains.
targetCustomer: Future industrial, robotics, engineering and biomedical AI developers
buyer: Future R&D, engineering and AI platform leaders; not yet validated
latestRound: $1.03B seed at a reported €3B valuation, March 2026
traction: The company was reported to have roughly ten employees at financing close and targets 30-50; no public product, customer or revenue evidence yet.
notes: Fact: AMI raised an exceptional seed round around Yann LeCun's world-model thesis. Inference: the technical opportunity is long-horizon predictive control beyond token models, but no product wedge is established. Unknown: architecture, training data, benchmark advantage, buyer urgency and commercialization timetable.

name: ElevenLabs
subsector: Audio foundation models and voice agents
product: Speech synthesis, dubbing, sound and music generation, transcription and production voice agents via API and applications.
targetCustomer: Developers, media and gaming companies, enterprises and creators
buyer: Product, contact-center, media, localization and engineering leaders; individual creators
traction: Company-reported annual recurring revenue exceeded $500M during the first four months of 2026, up from more than $330M for 2025.
notes: Fact: funding and ARR milestones are primary company disclosures; the team-size range uses a public report of roughly 400 people because LinkedIn's category appears stale. Inference: broad audio modalities, developer APIs and enterprise voice-agent workflows reinforce each other. Unknown: audited ARR, gross margin and concentration by use case.

name: DeepSeek
product: Open-weight language, reasoning and coding models plus consumer assistant and metered API.
buyer: Developers, AI platform leaders and individual users
fundingDisplay: More than RMB50B (about $7.4B) in a first external round reported in June 2026; company confirmation unavailable
investors: China National AI Industry Investment Fund
traction: Open-weight model releases achieved global developer distribution and a low-cost API; no reliable public revenue figure is available.
notes: Fact: model weights, technical reports and API documentation are public. Funding relies on Reuters reporting and was not confirmed by DeepSeek. The headcount range is stale, based on a January 2025 report of 139 researchers. Inference: algorithmic efficiency plus open distribution is the moat. Unknown: current staffing, revenue and investor allocation. Cross-border data, export-control and model-governance risk is material.

name: Moonshot AI (Kimi)
subsector: Open multimodal and coding foundation models
product: Kimi consumer assistant, open-weight language and multimodal models, coding agents and API services.
buyer: Individual users, developers and AI product leaders
fundingDisplay: $2B latest round in May 2026; lifetime funding not reliably consolidated
latestRound: $2B financing at a reported $20B valuation, May 2026
traction: TechCrunch reported annualized revenue above $200M in April 2026 based on a deal adviser; the figure is not a company filing.
notes: Fact: Kimi ships consumer, API and open-weight products, and Kimi-VL has a public technical report. Funding and revenue are credible secondary reports. Inference: open models plus a scaled consumer surface create a distribution flywheel. Unknown: audited revenue, cumulative funding and user retention. Cross-border data and model-governance risks are material.

name: MiniMax
subsector: Multimodal foundation models and consumer applications
product: Text, speech, music, image and video models delivered through APIs and consumer applications including Hailuo and Talkie.
buyer: Individual users, product, content and engineering leaders
fundingDisplay: HK$5.29B IPO proceeds reported in the 2025 annual report; pre-IPO lifetime funding not consolidated
traction: The annual report discloses 415 full-time and three part-time employees at year-end 2025; its prospectus records more than 10M monthly active users before the pre-B+ financing milestone.
notes: Fact: MiniMax is now public and publishes audited filings; IPO proceeds are not the same as lifetime venture funding. Inference: cross-modal model reuse across APIs and consumer products can create data and distribution advantages. Unknown: durable monetization by modality and international retention. China and cross-border content, data and export regulation remain material.

name: Z.ai (Zhipu AI)
subsector: GLM foundation models and enterprise MaaS
product: GLM language and multimodal models, coding and general agents, MaaS APIs and private enterprise deployments.
buyer: CIO, CTO, AI platform and engineering leaders; individual users
fundingDisplay: HK$4.17B estimated net IPO proceeds; pre-IPO lifetime funding not consolidated
traction: The prospectus reports 883 employees at June 2025, including 657 in R&D (74.4%), and a commercial stack spanning model APIs, agents and private deployment.
notes: Fact: Z.ai is public and the prospectus supplies staffing, offering and IPO data; IPO proceeds are not lifetime venture funding. Inference: deep enterprise deployment and local regulatory fit can be defensible within China. Unknown: international product-market fit and long-term margins. Cross-border data, content, export-control and procurement risk is material.
